clue.text: Support by lottery possibly a disadvantage

parts.note: a draw is a lottery, as in a prize draw
to back someone is to support them

explanation.surface: Funding something from lottery money might turn out to be a disadvantage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Support by lottery' puts BACK beside DRAW, with the lottery piece reading first.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawback is a snag or downside, a straightforward synonym for a disadvantage.

clue.text: Remove extremely disreputable model

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremities of the word, its first and last letters

parts.note: the two end letters of the word
a model poses, or strikes a pose

explanation.surface: A shady fashion model is being thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: To depose a ruler is to remove them from office, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Scared to help without brother in Italy

indicators.note: without is used in its old sense of outside, so one piece sits around the other

parts.note: aid is help
Fra is the Italian title for a friar or monastic brother

explanation.surface: Someone is too frightened to help a monk in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but in this older sense it means outside, so one piece is wrapped around the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Afraid and scared are plain synonyms for feeling fear.

clue.text: Reserve school for a literary gathering

parts.note: to book a table is to reserve it
a school, as of fish, is a group

explanation.surface: Someone is booking a school hall for a reading society.
explanation.walkthrough: School is not a place of learning here but a collective noun, as in a school of whales.
explanation.definitionFit: A book group is a club that meets to discuss books, so it is a gathering about literature.

clue.text: Kill retired Grand National winner pursuant to promise

indicators.note: pursuant to here means following on from, so one piece comes after the other

parts.note: to commit to something is to promise it

indicators.note: something retired has withdrawn or gone back, so the name is read from end to start

parts.note: Red Rum won the Grand National, Britain's famous steeplechase, three times

explanation.surface: A retired champion racehorse is about to be put down after a pledge.
explanation.walkthrough: Red Rum is the legendary horse that won the Grand National, a British steeplechase, in 1973, 1974 and 1977; turned round, its name gives MURDER, as in the film The Shining.
explanation.definitionFit: To commit murder is to kill someone deliberately, an idiom for the plain verb.

clue.text: Shocks hit dad, retrospectively

indicators.note: retrospectively means looking backwards, so the letters run in reverse order

parts.note: a slap is a hit
pa is an informal word for dad

explanation.surface: Someone is shocked, looking back, that they hit their father.
explanation.definitionFit: To appal someone is to shock or horrify them, a verb synonym in the same tense.

clue.text: Reportedly part of ending to the war

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard in a report, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a piece is a part, and it sounds identical to its twin spelling

explanation.surface: A news report on how a war might finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Peace is what follows when a war is over, so it describes the war's ending.

clue.text: About time unusual star act catches the eye

indicators.note: about means around, so the shuffled letters go around another piece
unusual means not in the normal form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A rare headline performance at last grabs the audience's attention.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters of 'star act' wrap the single letter for time.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that attracts draws attention to itself, which is what catching the eye means.

clue.text: Perspiring from consuming gutted sow earlier

indicators.note: earlier tells us this piece is placed in front of the other
gutted means with the insides removed, leaving only the outside letters

parts.note: the word with its middle letter removed
consuming food is eating it

explanation.surface: Someone is sweating after eating a sow that had been gutted.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweating is the everyday word for perspiring, same participle form.

clue.text: Theatrical company comes back and arranges plays

indicators.note: coming back means returning the way it came, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: rep is short for repertory, a theatre company
to form things is to arrange them

explanation.surface: A theatre troupe returns and sets up its plays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plays' looks like a plural noun matching the theatre surface, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To perform is to play, as a musician plays a piece, so the verbs match.

clue.text: Talked oddly after hit in fight

indicators.note: after places this piece behind the other

parts.note: to bat is to hit, as with a bat

indicators.note: oddly points to the odd-numbered positions in the word

parts.note: first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: Someone spoke strangely after taking a blow in a brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: A battle is a fight, a plain noun synonym.

clue.text: Absence of power to assist the French ship reach headland

parts.note: to assist is to help
le is French for the, in the masculine singular
SS stands for steamship
a ness is a headland or promontory, common in coastal place names

explanation.surface: A French ship is powerless to help as it reaches a headland.
explanation.walkthrough: Ness is a Scottish and English place-name word for a cape, as in Orford Ness.
explanation.definitionFit: Helplessness is the state of being unable to act, which is an absence of power.

clue.text: Piercing pain from cyst in groin

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow

parts.note: spans the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A sharp pain caused by a cyst in the groin.
explanation.walkthrough: The little word 'in' looks like a link but is part of the letter run.
explanation.definitionFit: A sting is a sharp, pricking pain, so a piercing pain is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Alien gent surprisingly lacking in refinement

indicators.note: surprisingly means in an unexpected way, so the letters fall into an unexpected order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A visiting gentleman from outer space turns out to have poor manners.
explanation.definitionFit: Inelegant means graceless or unpolished, which is lacking in refinement.

clue.text: Sophisticated women's magazine

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a long-running glossy magazine for women

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one description of a glossy magazine, but the adjective and the title are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A cosmopolitan person is worldly and urbane, and Cosmopolitan is also a famous monthly women's magazine.

clue.text: In cryptic clues, hero is lustful

indicators.note: cryptic means puzzling or obscure, so the letters are scrambled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A wry aside that in crosswords the hero always turns out to be lecherous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cryptic clues' reads as a phrase about crosswords, but 'cryptic' acts on the two words that follow it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lecherous describes someone with excessive sexual desire, a synonym for lustful.

clue.text: Reserve detective takes position

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector
a stance is a position or posture

explanation.surface: A backup detective is taking up a post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reserve' reads as a substitute or a verb, but here it is a noun meaning aloofness.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping one's distance means being cool and aloof, the same sense as showing reserve.

clue.text: Animal on island to the north can be tolerated

indicators.note: in a down entry, on means placed above, so this piece sits on top

parts.note: a bear is an animal

indicators.note: in a down entry, going north means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: Elba is the island where Napoleon was exiled

explanation.surface: A wild animal on a northern island is something you can put up with.
explanation.definitionFit: Bearable means endurable, so it describes what can be tolerated.

clue.text: Lack of practical knowledge starts off international nuclear event

indicators.note: starts off means the opening letters are taken from the words that follow

parts.note: the opening letter of each word
an experience is an event someone goes through

explanation.surface: Ignorance sets off a global nuclear incident.
explanation.definitionFit: Inexperience is not having done something before, so a want of hands-on know-how.

clue.text: Some superstar vegans go very hungry

indicators.note: some means only a part, so the letters are a portion of the words that follow

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Celebrity vegans are going without food.
explanation.definitionFit: To starve is to suffer severe hunger, a verb equal to going very hungry.

clue.text: Take a b-break

parts.note: taken as written
a break is a rest, and the stammered first letter shown in the clue is copied onto that synonym

explanation.surface: A stammering suggestion to stop for a breather.
explanation.walkthrough: The stutter on 'break' tells you to stutter its synonym the same way: a rest becomes a r-rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a suspect is to arrest them, as police take someone into custody.

clue.text: Jeopardises the rents with a review

indicators.note: a review reworks something, so the letters are recast in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written, joining the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A rent review puts tenants' security at risk.
explanation.definitionFit: To threaten something is to put it in danger, which is what jeopardises means.

clue.text: Examine car before end of MOT

indicators.note: before places this piece in front of the other

parts.note: an Audi is a make of car

indicators.note: end of points to the final letter of the following word

parts.note: the final letter

explanation.surface: Checking over a car before its MOT ends.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOT is Britain's annual roadworthiness test for cars.
explanation.definitionFit: An audit is a formal inspection, so to audit is to examine closely.

clue.text: Come into business with 50% reduction

indicators.note: a 50% reduction cuts away half, so only the first half of the word stays

parts.note: an enterprise is a business

explanation.surface: Joining a firm that is offering half price.
explanation.walkthrough: The business word has ten letters, so halving it keeps the first five.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter a room is to come into it, a plain verb synonym.

clue.text: Unlikely outcome to bumping off an unimportant person

definitions.note: read as two words, no body
definitions.meaning: first meaning, split in two: after a murder you would expect a corpse, so not having one is unusual
second meaning: someone of no significance

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a whimsical cryptic definition: split the answer in two and it says there is no corpse, odd after bumping someone off (killing them).
explanation.definitionFit: A nobody is a person of no standing or importance, a noun used just like that.

clue.text: Soldiers have gone off with church fund

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers
milk that has gone off has turned sour
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Troops have walked off with the church's money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gone off' suggests departing, but here it describes spoiled food.
explanation.definitionFit: A resource is a supply or stock to draw on, which is what a fund is.

clue.text: Sets up son after Queen's shocking treatment

indicators.note: after places the first-mentioned piece behind the others

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen
ECT is electroconvulsive therapy, a treatment using electric shocks
S is the standard abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A son arranges matters after the monarch's scandalous treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shocking' suggests scandal but is literal: electric shocks.
explanation.definitionFit: To erect a structure is to set it up or build it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: In my view, it's possibly easiest to include setter

indicators.note: to include means to hold inside, so the shuffled letters surround another piece
possibly suggests one of several arrangements, so the letters may be reordered

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
the setter refers to themselves as I

explanation.surface: The setter's opinion on the simplest approach.
explanation.definitionFit: As I see it is an idiom introducing a personal opinion, the same as saying in my view.
